primary.title: The Republic
primary.author: Plato
primary.rationale: Plato's most famous and influential work, exploring justice, the ideal state, and the theory of Forms.

primary.title: Apology
primary.author: Plato
primary.rationale: A defense of Socrates, presented by Plato, offering insights into Socrates' philosophy and trial.

primary.title: Symposium
primary.author: Plato
primary.rationale: A dialogue exploring the nature of love (Eros), featuring speeches by various characters.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Plato
secondary.author: Richard Kraut
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Plato's philosophy and works.

secondary.title: Plato: A Very Short Introduction
secondary.author: Julia Annas
secondary.rationale: A concise and accessible overview of Plato's life, thought, and major works, suitable for introductory research.

secondary.title: Plato's Republic: A Philosophical Commentary
secondary.author: R. C. Cross and A. D. Woozley
secondary.rationale: While slightly before the 1976 cutoff, this is a foundational scholarly commentary on The Republic that remains highly relevant and frequently cited in later scholarship.

suggestions.notes: Plato's dialogues are the primary source of his philosophy. The dates provided for primary sources are approximate and refer to the likely period of composition.
